decisions.summary: The record first: the village-lanes entry rewritten from what was read (brief R1); the drawing page (brief R2) once D2-D4 land
decisions.why: FR-001 and US1 as written.

decisions.summary: A household asks for a corridor first; only where access_corridor finds none may it be reached by passage
decisions.why: Unchanged ruling: implied by the GM's 'if that is what the research bears out, then we should go with it' - every Wigmore entry conditions passage on land that 'cannot reach the highway without passing over' another's; no unresearched requirement is added.

decisions.summary: While the share has room, standing houses offer tight seats at the footprints' parting plus 2 px, without the path's strip
decisions.why: The mechanism the MODE 1 ruling of 2026-10-03 required so that FR-002's 'MUST be able to seat' can happen; bounded by D4's share.

decisions.summary: A tight seat is taken only by passage; a household finding its own corridor there is refused it; ordinary seats keep a path's room
decisions.why: Excludes no household that could be reached across a yard; lane households keep the spacing the spec does not ask to change. D2-order applied at the tight seat.

decisions.summary: Tight seats offered only round a house a passage may cross to: reached within D3's chain and with a yard (passage.crossable)
decisions.why: A tight seat is taken only by passage (D2-tight-refusal), and a passage must end at a neighbor's yard whose house reaches the tree within PASSAGE_CHAIN (D2-walk, D3). A tight seat round any other house could seat no one, so the filter removes only seats that could never be taken; no household FR-002 allows is excluded.

decisions.summary: Tight seats offered only within TIGHT_BEARING_DEG 90 (was 112.5) of the bearing from the house to its yard, the side its yard lies on, as the drawing page places it
decisions.why: A narrowing, ruled as before: the research's condition says nothing of which side of the neighbor's house the land lies. Legitimate on the spec's OWN rules, not on cost: FR-002 forbids the walk crossing a house, bed, shed or fixture and D2-walk keeps it on the two households' land, so the excluded sector is all but emptied by FR-002 itself (R7, every bearing offered: 15 of 16 passages within 90 degrees, 1 walk in 194 tries behind). The move from 112.5 to 90 is held to the record's own drawing page, labeled a map drawing convention, and growth.py's comment records 23 passage households at 15 households, seeds 1-16, at either value - no passage lost on the measured run. A household outside the band is still seated with its own way; US2's purpose is not gutted.

decisions.summary: No tight seat offered within TIGHT_TREE_FT (80 ft) of the access tree
decisions.why: A narrowing: it is a distance proxy for the custom's condition, not the condition, so in principle a household near the tree that is nonetheless shut in by its neighbors could no longer be reached by passage; the record says nothing of distance to a way. Legitimate on the same ground as D2-tight-yard-side: the excluded zone is emptied by the request's own research condition as D2-order applies it (a household with a way of its own is not land the custom covers). Measured (R8, 15 households, 13 settlements): no passage from nearer than 87 ft; of 135 of 343 tight tries nearer than 80 ft, every walk found (9 of 9) had a corridor of its own - so the cut removes no household the custom covers on the measured run, and passages remain (7 at 15 households, 8 at 40). It is not a historical claim and must not be recorded as one (the constant's comment and R2 brief: a search breadth, measured). Caveat for the record: R8 measured it at 15 households only; the plan's sentence omits that scope.

decisions.summary: Once one garden layout at a tight seat finds a corridor, the seat's other layouts are refused unasked
decisions.why: Legitimate on the same ground as D2-order: Wigmore's condition is the LAND's - land that cannot reach the highway without passing over another's - and a seat from which some garden layout has a way of its own is land with road access. The previous round's item (93 of 106 not in R7) is closed: R7 now records 106 found, 93 corridors after a walk. Now subsumed by D2-land.

decisions.summary: The reach is the custom's condition: the household's land (the reach its seat was parted by, over every layout) within the parting and PASSAGE_ADJOIN_FT of the neighbor's footprint, a GUESS
decisions.why: Unchanged: land against land, the spec's 'across a neighbor's dooryard' read literally; makes FR-002 reachable rather than restricting it (R6).

decisions.summary: The walk from a dooryard door to the neighbor's threshing yard, on the two households' land, clear of houses, beds, sheds, byres, well pockets, fixtures, other homesteads, refused ground and wood seats, routed; not drawn as a lane (GUESS)
decisions.why: Unchanged: FR-002's clearances and US2's 'no lane of its own'; routing removes a restriction the request never asked for (R6).

decisions.summary: At a tight seat the walk is asked first, then the corridor; the same verdict
decisions.why: Unchanged: evaluation order with an identical verdict.

decisions.summary: THE LAND, NOT ONE LAYOUT (passage.landlocked): a tight seat is taken only where some layout has a walk and none has a corridor of its own, asked once a seat before any layout is judged
decisions.why: A narrowing of what the engine admits (R8: 13 -> 7 passages at 15 households; 20 -> 8 at 40), but not of what was asked: request.md says 'if that is what the research bears out, then we should go with it', and every Wigmore entry the spec cites conditions passage on LAND that 'cannot reach the highway without passing over' another's. A household one of whose garden layouts has a way of its own is on land with road access; admitting it because the first layout tried blocked its own path made the passage depend on evaluation order, which the research does not support. This completes D2-own-way (ruled LEGITIMATE) rather than adding a new limit, and R8 shows the 13 earlier passage households all reached the tree round their house alone (house_reaches) - none was shut in by neighbors. FR-002's 'MUST be able to seat' still holds (7 and 8 passages). Not cost-motivated.

decisions.summary: ON THE FINISHED SEATING (passage.recheck_passages): once all are seated, each passage household is asked again, its homestead set aside, whether it has a corridor of its own; one that has is seated by it and loses its passage (meta.passage_revoked)
decisions.why: Narrows what the engine admits (R9: 23 -> 15 passage households at 15 households, band and recheck together), not what was asked: the GM's 'if that is what the research bears out, then we should go with it', and every Wigmore entry conditions passage on land that cannot reach the highway without passing over another's. A household with a drawn lane a few feet off (Inashiro, the farmhouse glyph check F5) is not land the custom covers. Same ground as D2-order and D2-land; FR-002's 'MUST be able to seat' still holds (15 and 12).

decisions.summary: Accepted limitation: the recheck asks only the layout drawn, where the seat asked every layout; another layout at the seat would give a way of its own to 2 of 15 passage households at 15 households and 3 of 12 at 40 (R9); accepted for this landing and put to the GM
decisions.why: An exception carved from the plan's own D2-land rule (ruled LEGITIMATE precisely because the research's condition is the LAND's: 'a household lays its beds where its way can run') and from FR-007 / the GM's 'I do want all known bugs to be fixed'. The impl-drift check returned it DRIFTED against the drawing page's 'if any layout of the homestead would leave it a way of its own, it has one', which the page calls historically accurate. So 2 of 15 and 3 of 12 finished maps draw the custom where the research says it does not apply - the passage going beyond 'what the research bears out', the reverse of the request's purpose. None of the legitimating grounds holds: not physically impossible (R9 itself names the fix - re-lay the household with the layout that has a way, in the engine's one guarded place, _solve_homestead - or unseat and re-seat it); not implied by the GM's words; honoring the rule serves the request's purpose rather than defeating it. The reasons given are cost: an in-place re-lay is work, and recording a drawn-layout deviation re-owes ~300 claims. 'This will be hard' is not a fidelity ground, and recording a deviation from the research for cost would not be 'go with it' either. The plan should say: on the finished seating every layout at a passage household's seat is asked, as landlocked asks at the seat; a household with a way of its own under any layout is given it (re-laid or re-seated) and loses its passage; measured 0 such households on the reference at 15 and 40. If that proves impossible, an impossibility investigation goes to the GM before landing, not after.

decisions.summary: A chain of passages ends at a corridor within PASSAGE_CHAIN = 2, a GUESS citing Echigo
decisions.why: Unchanged: the spec delegates any chain limit to the plan as a labeled GUESS citing Echigo.

decisions.summary: PASSAGE_SHARE_BAND = (0.0, 0.25) rolled per nucleated settlement, a GUESS; beyond the share only with a corridor
decisions.why: Unchanged: FR-002's rolled share within a band labeled as a guess.

decisions.summary: reached_across on the record; checks.unreached_houses counts a chain ending at a reached household
decisions.why: FR-003 as written.

decisions.summary: The ways owe a household reached across a yard no lane of its own: arm/fragment keeping, carried ends and the web's cut spacing ask geom.lane_houses (every farmhouse but those reached across a neighbor's yard); an end that merely reaches a house still counts every house
decisions.why: US2 as written: 'A household so reached has no lane of its own'; FR-003 is carried by the passage chain (D5). Without it the ways would build the very lane the spec says such a household lacks.

decisions.summary: The household a passage is reached across keeps its corridor: owed and never pruned however near the lanes its center stands (tree.passage_anchors; Inashiro glyph-check F1)
decisions.why: Serves FR-002 ('to a way') and FR-003: a passage that ends at a yard whose own house has no drawn way leaves the chain ending at nothing (R8, the anchor 90 ft from a lane, two farmsteads with no way). It adds a corridor only for a household another is reached across; no household that may be reached by passage is excluded and no lane is imposed on any other house, so the GM's purpose (no unresearched lane-to-every-house requirement) is untouched.

decisions.summary: The corridor judged as drawn (tree.as_joined, the exact box prefilter in law.near_misses / law.free_end); the judge's own_clear / tree.laid_run defect (seed 18) kept closed; a joint's pull never taken into a kink (seed 47 at 20 hh)
decisions.why: FR-004 and SC-003 as written; seed 18's judge defect and seed 47's WebRefused are bugs found against main, closed under FR-005 and FR-007 ('a bug found later joins the list'). None changes who may be reached or how.

decisions.summary: The route searched per garden layout round the household's own parts retried and WITHDRAWN: after feature 315 merged it cost the homesteads stage 3-43% more in calls than main's search round the house alone (R8); the corridor's route keeps off the house alone, as on main
decisions.why: The plan's own condition ('kept only if it pays', FR-006) applied as written. No FR requires the per-layout route; withdrawing it returns to main's behavior, so no household is lost against main (FR-005). It does not cut against the request's purpose: the GM asked that we not disregard 'optimizations that we know work' for an unresearched requirement, and R8 measures this one as no longer working (4.72M/3.26M/15.52M/3.48M calls against main's 4.59M/2.99M/11.64M/2.43M, re-derived: +2.8%, +9.0%, +33.3%, +43.2%); it is withdrawn on its cost, not to protect a requirement. The house_reaches shortcut and the persimmon-out-of-obstacles change that served it leave the plan with it.

decisions.summary: Known bugs listed with owners: D6 here; cohort seeds 14, 15, 906, 22, 23 with the Diagram (Inashiro) session
Feature 315's persimmon reseat asks a neighbor's sun of every seat it tries, on the rolled side and then the other (persimmon_reseat.persimmon_for); Inashiro 11 -> 12 of 12 rolled (B10)
decisions.why: A regression this feature's tight seats exposed on a pool map (FR-005: no pool map may fail a rule it passed before) and a bug found at the gate (FR-007 joins the list). The reseat serves a tree the hamlet's count rolled to a household that rolled none; trying the other side of the house keeps the tree in its dooryard (feature 315's rule) and the count whole, and relaxes nothing the GM's request or this spec set. Not a narrowing: it admits more, not less. The tried alternative (refusing a tight seat that dropped its persimmon) would have narrowed passages and was reverted.

decisions.why: FR-007: a known bug found by the impl-drift check, fixed in the work at hand.
